minor.issue: Pydantic body validation runs before RBAC dependency in FastAPI's request pipeline: an empty body returns 422 (Unprocessable Entity) instead of 403 for an unauthorized client. With a body that passes min-length validation (final_title>=2, statement>=10) the endpoint correctly returns 403. Cosmetic concern only — no security gap (the role check eventually fires before any DB write). To get 403 first, declare the role-check dependency before the Body(...) parameter or run it inside a Depends() that wraps the body.

rca of the issue: No blocking issues. Two cosmetic findings: (a) POST /api/journeys/{jid}/certify-closure returns 422 (Pydantic body validation) before 403 (RBAC) when called with an empty/invalid body — FastAPI runs request body parsing before Depends() role checks by default. With a valid body, 403 is correctly returned. To prefer 403-first, move role-check into a Depends() invoked BEFORE the Body(...) parameter, or use an APIRouter dependency. No security risk because role check still fires before any DB mutation. (b) The substring 'celebrazione' appears in JourneyClosureCeremony.jsx but only inside the meta-copy 'Tono editoriale, sobrio, atemporale. Nessuna celebrazione, nessun [...]' (explicitly negating celebration). Static pytest test_router_zero_celebratory_vocabulary scans the router (not the JSX); the JSX intentionally references the forbidden vocabulary in a negating sentence. Not a violation.
